MC	<p>abd9_d014</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c41b2;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6c41b2;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c41b2;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hy, ++, hy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>d26d_6fdf</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006a7a;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a7a;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a7a;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973070;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #973070;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5600;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c5fa6;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1c5fa6;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>e435_3de8</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b1e;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236c54;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #236c54;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>8fd3_fa4a</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3b1e;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #216f2d;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #216f2d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c5fa6;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1c5fa6;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>0d11_fb59</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7c5600;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7c5600;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5600;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, et, ++, et"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a02e45;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206587;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #206587;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>cd2a_d014</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973070;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #973070;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct
MC	<p>444a_4950</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #216f2d;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #216f2d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #216f2d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973070;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #973070;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>adec_d1ab</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3b1e;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #444fc0;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #444fc0;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>6ab4_bd51</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b1e;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #216f2d;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #216f2d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct
MC	<p>7953_46eb</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b1e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kt, ++, kt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a7a;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a7a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>2d75_46ca</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b1e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236c54;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #236c54;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206587;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #206587;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>12c1_facb</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b1e;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a7a;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a7a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>9d73_e4e6</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b1e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236c54;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973070;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #973070;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>b457_656b</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #216f2d;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #216f2d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #216f2d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #444fc0;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #444fc0;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #444fc0;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kw, ++, kw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a02e45;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a7a;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006a7a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes. Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">8,800</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row with the Parental Type for both genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Assign PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b1e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236c54;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #236c54;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct
MC	<p>2c95_d1ab</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c0e;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8a4c0e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c0e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a7a;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a7a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype.
